tone.target: aggressive British metal intro with tight palm-muted crunch and high-end bite
tone.profile: aggressive British metal intro with tight palm-muted crunch and high-end bite
tone.summary: A high-gain signal chain utilizing a Boost/OD for initial bite, followed by the UK 45 amp model and UK Vintage 4x12 cab to achieve tight, punchy metal riffing with bright upper mids.
corrections: lean more JCM/plexi crunch than modern high gain

rig.name: Judas Priest - The Hellion - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up high-gain noise and maintain tight riff articulation.
Provide initial aggressive bite and tighten the attack for palm-muted chugs.
blocks.gap: The Boost is used here to simulate a slight overdrive boost, enhancing the upper mids without adding excessive grit.

alternatives.reason: A Green OD could also provide bite, but 'Boost' offers more control for pure tightening.

blocks.purpose: Add aggressive crunch and mid-range punch characteristic of classic metal tones.
blocks.gap: The RAT-style is chosen for its tight, biting character, fitting the 'metal riff punch' requirement better than a Muff or Chief.

alternatives.reason: Could work, but might be too scooped compared to the RAT-style for this specific aggressive tone.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Marshall-style British crunch and punch required for Judas Priest's sound.
Provide the classic British cabinet sound and necessary high-end clarity.
Enhance the upper mids and overall bite while controlling low-end muddiness.
blocks.gap: Using EQ 2 allows for more precise mid-range sculpting to achieve the 'bright upper mids' required.

alternatives.reason: Could work, but EQ 2 offers better control for aggressive tone shaping.

blocks.purpose: Placeholder for minimal effects; kept off to maintain maximum tightness and dryness.
blocks.gap: No modulation is needed, but a placeholder block is required. Chorus is the least intrusive option when bypassed.

blocks.purpose: Placeholder for minimal effects; kept off to maintain maximum tightness and dryness.
blocks.gap: No delay is needed, but a placeholder block is required. Digital Delay is the most versatile option when bypassed.

blocks.purpose: Add a subtle sense of space without sounding 'lush' or muddy.
blocks.gap: The reverb is kept very low (10% mix) to satisfy the requirement for minimal effects while adding necessary depth.

alternatives.reason: Could be used, but Room provides a more natural, less artificial sense of space for metal.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR for increased cabinet realism and high-end bite.

proposals.reason: Enhance the perceived depth and realism of the Marshall-style cab sound.
